root_cause: A systematic orientation/axis-mapping error exists between the Meteosat and EPIC cloud masks. Applying a 180-degree rotation to one mask raises agreement from 0.537 to 0.798, exceeding the 0.75 quality threshold.

recommended_repair.action: Apply a 180-degree rotation to one of the cloud masks before comparison, or correct the underlying axis/orientation mapping in the comparison pipeline.

remaining_uncertainty: The exact source of the orientation error (e.g., which mask is inverted, or whether a transpose or flip is also needed) is not fully isolated; only rot180 was tested.
Whether the 0.798 agreement is the maximum achievable or whether other transformations (rot90, rot270, flips) yield even higher agreement remains untested.

evidence_summary.final_inference: A systematic orientation/axis-mapping error exists between the Meteosat and EPIC cloud masks. Applying a 180-degree rotation to one mask raises agreement from 0.537 to 0.798, exceeding the 0.75 quality threshold.
